domain_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me check domain name availability across multiple TLDs using Name.com. If you don't already have the following from me, ask first:

1. A list of 2-5 candidate brand/business names (base names, no TLD) I want to check.
2. The list of TLDs I want checked (e.g. .com, .io, .co, .ai, .net) — if I haven't given you one, propose a sensible default set of 6-8 common/relevant TLDs and confirm with me before proceeding.

Once you have the names and TLD list, use your configured Name.com credentials to check availability for every combination of candidate name + TLD via the Name.com dashboard or API's domain availability lookup. For each combination, record whether it is available, taken, or premium-priced (and note the premium price if shown).

Compile the results into a single organized table with columns: Candidate Name, TLD, Status (Available / Taken / Premium), Price (if premium or if a standard price is shown). Sort the table so available domains appear first, grouped by candidate name.

Done looks like: every requested name/TLD combination has a checked status, and I have a complete table with no missing rows.

Report back to me with:
- The full results table
- A short summary highlighting which candidate names have their .com (or top-priority TLD) available
- Any premium-priced domains flagged clearly with their price
- Any combinations that could not be checked due to errors, listed separately so I know what needs manual follow-up

Do not register or purchase any domain — this step is availability-checking only.

domain_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me check whether my desired brand/company name is available as a matching handle across major social and developer platforms, so I can confirm consistent branding alongside my domain search.

First, ask me for: (1) the exact name or short list of name variants I want checked (e.g., the base name plus reasonable variants like with underscores, dots, or a suffix like 'hq' or 'app'), and (2) which platforms matter most to me if I have preferences — otherwise default to checking X (Twitter), Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn (company page), GitHub, and Reddit.

For each name variant and each platform, check whether the handle/username is already taken by visiting the platform's public profile URL or using its in-app username/availability check (e.g., navigating to the profile path for that username and observing whether a profile exists or a 'not found'/'available' signal appears). Do not create accounts, sign up, or claim any handle — this remains a human step.

Compile results into a simple table: rows = name variants, columns = platforms, cells = 'Available', 'Taken', or 'Unclear' (if the check was ambiguous or blocked, e.g., by a login wall). Note any platform where you could not get a reliable read.

When done, report back: the full table, a short summary of which name variant has the best overall availability across platforms, and a flagged list of any platforms/variants that need me to verify manually (e.g., due to login walls or CAPTCHAs). Do not attempt to register, purchase, or reserve any handle — just report availability findings for my review.

domain_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me shortlist domain name candidates for my startup, including pricing and renewal costs. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) a list of candidate brand/domain names or root words to check, (2) preferred TLDs to prioritize (e.g., .com, .io, .ai, .co, .dev), and (3) any budget ceiling per year I want to stay under.

Once you have these, use web search or browser tools to check availability and pricing for each candidate name across the requested TLDs. Check pricing and renewal rates directly on registrar sites such as Namecheap, GoDaddy, Porkbun, Google Domains successor (Squarespace Domains), or Cloudflare Registrar — compare at least two to three registrars for accuracy, since first-year promotional pricing often differs sharply from renewal pricing.

For each candidate/TLD combination, record: availability status (available, taken, premium-priced), first-year registration price, standard renewal price (this is the more important number long-term), and which registrar quoted that price. Flag any domains marked as "premium" since these often carry unusually high renewal costs.

Compile the results into a clear table or list sorted by relevance (e.g., .com first, then other TLDs), showing name, TLD, availability, first-year price, renewal price, and source registrar. Highlight any renewal costs that seem unusually high relative to registration price.

Done looks like: a shortlist covering every candidate name across the requested TLDs, each with availability and both first-year and renewal pricing clearly documented, ready for me to review and pick a final domain. Report back the full table plus a short summary noting the best value options and any red flags on renewal pricing.
